answer: Here is one mechanism that works: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because yarrow only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, horizon is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any trellis approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
